indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.1.1.1: Show understanding of the physical features and life processes of living things and use this understanding to classify them
indicator.objective: Classify living things into plants and animals by their life processes

skills.description: Identify a given living thing as a plant or an animal
Recognise key features/life processes used to classify them
Choose the best reason why a living thing is classified as a plant or an animal based on its life processes
Sort a small group of living things into plants and animals

misconceptions: Anything that moves is an animal, and anything that does not move is a plant.
Plants are not living things because they do not eat food like us.
Seaweed and water lilies are animals because they live in water.
Trees are not plants; they are just wood.

questions.stem: Which of these living things is a plant?
questions.explanation: A mango tree is a plant because it has roots, a stem, and leaves, and it makes its own food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think anything green is just a decoration, not a living plant.

questions.stem: Which of these living things is an animal?
hints: It moves around and eats food.
It has four legs and gives milk.
questions.explanation: A cow is an animal because it moves, eats food, and breathes.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think animals must be wild.

questions.stem: Is a fish a plant or an animal?
hints: It does not have roots or leaves.
questions.explanation: A fish is an animal because it moves, eats, and breathes (using gills).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fish are not animals because they live in water.

questions.stem: Which of these features is usually found in plants but NOT in animals?
questions.explanation: Roots are a feature of plants that help them take in water and stay in the soil.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think animals have roots.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT an animal?
hints: It does not move from place to place.
questions.explanation: A rose plant is a plant, not an animal. It has roots, leaves, and flowers.
questions.misconception: Pupils may classify a rose as an animal because it is colourful.

questions.stem: Which life process helps us tell that a plant is a living thing?
hints: Plants use sunlight to make food.
questions.explanation: Plants are living things because they make their own food, grow, and reproduce, even though they do not run or talk.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think plants are non-living because they do not move.

questions.stem: Why is a dog classified as an animal?
options: Because it can move and eat food
hints: Think about what it does to stay alive.
questions.explanation: A dog is an animal because it moves, eats food, breathes, and reproduces.
questions.misconception: Pupils may classify by colour or size instead of life processes.

questions.stem: Which group has ONLY plants?
hints: Which group has things that grow in the soil and have leaves?
questions.explanation: Maize, grass, and a pawpaw tree are all plants.
questions.misconception: Pupils may put a goat in the plant group because it eats grass.

questions.stem: Ama says 'A stone is a plant because it does not move.' Why is she wrong?
options: A stone cannot grow or make food; it is non-living, not a plant
A stone is a type of plant
A stone is a living thing
questions.explanation: A stone is non-living, not a plant. Plants are living things that grow and make food.
questions.misconception: Pupils often think anything that does not move is a plant.

questions.stem: Which of these life processes is common to BOTH plants and animals?
options: They both make their own food
hints: Do both get bigger over time?
questions.explanation: Both plants and animals grow. They are both living things.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think plants do not grow.

questions.stem: Sort these into plants and animals: goat, maize, fish, orange tree.
answer: plants: maize, orange tree; animals: goat, fish
hints: Which two have leaves and roots?
questions.explanation: Maize and the orange tree are plants. The goat and fish are animals.
questions.misconception: Pupils may struggle with the fish because it lives in water.

questions.stem: Give one reason why a mango tree is a plant and not an animal.
answer: it does not move from place to place
hints: Where does it get its food?
questions.explanation: A mango tree is a plant because it has roots, makes its own food, and does not move from place to place.
questions.misconception: Pupils may focus on what it produces (mangoes) rather than its features.

questions.stem: Why is a frog classified as an animal, even though it can live in water?
options: It moves, eats food, and breathes
hints: Think about what makes an animal an animal.
questions.explanation: A frog is an animal because it is a living thing that moves, eats food, and breathes, regardless of where it lives.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water-dwelling creatures are not animals.

questions.stem: Which of these sets of features best describes an animal?
options: Has roots, makes food, stays in one place
Has leaves, grows tall, needs sunlight
Has a stem, flowers, and roots
hints: Think about how animals get their food.
questions.explanation: Animals move around, eat food, and breathe. The other options describe plants.
questions.misconception: Pupils may mix up plant and animal features.

questions.stem: Kofi finds an organism that grows in the soil, has green leaves, and does not move from place to place. How should he classify it?
hints: It has leaves and grows in the soil.
These are features of a plant.
questions.explanation: Organisms that grow in the soil, have green leaves, and do not move are classified as plants.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think it is non-living because it does not move.

questions.stem: Ama has four pictures: a dog, a seaweed, a cow, and a water lily. Which are the plants?
hints: Which ones make their own food and have roots/leaves?
Which ones live in water but are still plants?
questions.explanation: Seaweed and water lilies are plants, even though they live in water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all water-dwelling things are animals.

questions.stem: Write down two features that tell you a living thing is a plant.

criteria.description: States a correct plant feature (e.g., has roots, leaves, makes its own food)
States a second correct plant feature

questions.explanation: Plants have roots, stems, leaves, and make their own food using sunlight.

questions.stem: Ama says 'A moving car is an animal because it moves.' Why is she wrong?
options: A car cannot grow, eat, or breathe
hints: Can a car make baby cars?
questions.explanation: A car is non-living. Even though it moves, it cannot grow, eat, breathe, or reproduce like an animal.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think movement is the only sign of life.

questions.stem: Explain why a fish is an animal even though it lives in water.

criteria.description: States that it moves and eats food
States that it breathes (using gills) and is a living thing

questions.explanation: A fish is an animal because it is a living thing that moves, eats, and breathes, even though it lives in water.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher one plant and one animal you can see in your community, and explain how you know which is which.

criteria.description: Names a plant and an animal
Explains a correct feature for each (e.g., plant has leaves/roots, animal moves/eats)

hints: Does it move? Does it have leaves?
questions.explanation: This tests the ability to classify using observable features.
